shortDescription: The Czech National Bank (CNB) could raise interest rates further if demand and lending pressures remain and external cost shocks persist, the bank said in the minutes of its last policy meeting on September 17, published on Friday.

children: The Czech National Bank (CNB) could raise interest rates further if demand and lending pressures remain and external cost shocks persist, the bank said in the minutes of its last policy meeting on September 17, published on Friday.

The CNB left its main repo rate (CZCBIR=ECI) unchanged at 3.75% at that gathering, but said a hike would be considered at the next meeting in November. It has said a June rate hike had given it room to assess incoming data.

"There was a consensus in the (meeting's) discussion that growth in market rates with longer maturities had led to an autonomous tightening of financial conditions," the minutes also said, adding this factor combined with the June hike and the still strong crown provided it space.
"If domestic demand proved resilient, lending remained strong and the external cost shock persisted, the appropriate response by the central bank could be to raise interest rates slightly further."
Governor Ales Michl said after the meeting this month that most of the debate was about domestic inflation pressures.
Inflation (CZCPIY=ECI) has been below the bank's 2% target for much of this year but core inflation is still running hot, with risks from wages, lending and service sector price growth.
Conflict in the Middle East this year has hit global energy markets, but the board said in the minutes no second-round effects on consumers were seen yet from the energy shock.

However, Vice-Governor Jan Frait, according to the minutes, said the conflict had become a source of another cost shock with gas and electricity prices following oil up, and the impact could be longer-lasting.
Vice-Governor Eva Zamrazilova said second-round effects could soon show up in core inflation with the conflict dragging on, and that was a risk to achieving the inflation target, the minutes showed.
